tasks.desc: Resident consumers publish and heartbeat their OWN consumer-capable thread
tasks.acceptance: the wake watcher never borrows resident capability; a resident that stops publishing stops being credited
tasks.note: codex-pantheon's ruling, adopted. gemma-pantheon's health check is `sirsi-gemma-worker.sh --version` — it proves a binary can print a string, not that a consumer is alive. Changes the thread model, so it ships separately. DONE 2026-08-06: `thread register --consumer-capable` is the publish side — guarded so only an agent declaring consumer.mode=resident may claim it, and RegisterThread's reuse path now RAISES the flag so a live worker can promote an already-minted record. Credit lapses by going stale in WakePass's armed predicate; nothing clears it. | DONE 2026-08-06 PR #599: resident credited only on a thread it published itself (active, heartbeat-fresh, ConsumerCapable). health_check demoted to optional/disqualifying-only — a passing probe can no longer qualify a lane. Credit now decays via DefaultThreadStaleAfter. Falsified both directions. | COMPLETED BY PR #598: the PUBLISH half. #599 tightened the CONSUME side (credit only on a published thread) but nothing on main could SET ConsumerCapable for a resident — wake.go refuses by design and no CLI could publish it — so residents were temporarily uncreditable. #598 adds `thread register --consumer-capable`, guarded to agents declaring consumer.mode=resident, and raises the flag in BOTH RegisterThread reuse branches. Raise-only is safe because WakePass:404 drops stale threads before the IsInboxConsumer check, so credit lapses on its own.
